newsitem.title: CANADA: New Emery air chief eyes widebody freighters.
newsitem.headline: New Emery air chief eyes widebody freighters.

text.p: U.S. integrated freight carrier Emery Worldwide will move quickly on a decision to add widebody freighter aircraft to its domestic fleet, said Kent Scott, new head of airline operations.

"It's one of my highest priorities and one we are going to put a lot of effort into in the very, very near term," Scott told Reuters on his third day on the job as chief operating officer of Emery Worldwide Airlines.
He said a move by Emery into widebodies is overdue.
"We probably could have used widebodies in the last year, or even two," he said in a telephone interview.
"We think Emery is perfectly positioned to be a very good user of widebody aircraft."
Widebodies will be used mainly for growth -- to take the carrier "to the next level", said Scott -- and for fleet renewal.
"We're straining at the seams. We know we have to get more capacity just to keep up with the current business."

The company prefers used freighters to new. In all likelihood, Emery will look at converted passenger McDonnell Douglas DC-10s or Lockheed L-1011s, he said. Either would have more capacity than the narrowbody DC-8s which are the mainstay of Emery's current fleet.

Scott, 53, a former Trans World Airlines Boeing 747 captain, dismissed the Boeing 767-200 as well as the Airbus candidates - the A300B2/B4. He also said the 747, darling of intercontinental operators, was too large for domestic requirements.

The DC-10s may be the best aircraft, but are in short supply. L-1011s carry less than DC-10s, but are in greater supply, "and at the price tag they are out there being offered at right now, we have to take a serious look at those," said Scott.
Widebodies would take over some high demand corridors from the airline's Dayton, Ohio hub, he said.

Emery's fleet includes 39 DC-8 freighters of various types, only 21 of which are the update -71 and -73 variants, re-engined in the last decade and in compliance with all actual or pending noise-abatement rules.
Emery also uses 38 narrowbody aircraft - mainly B-727s - in its domestic freight and postal operations.
Internationally, where Emery functions as a freight forwarder, the airline uses other carriers for lift and doesn't yet have a need for dedicated aircraft, said Scott.
Talk of Emery diversifying into widebody aircraft has been around the company for years. Now, some of its U.S. rivals are making aggressive fleet expansion moves.
DHL Airways, with a similar fleet profile as Emery, announced this week it is buying seven ex-Thai Airways A300B2 aircraft from Airbus for delivery in 1998 and 1999.

Airborne Express is acquiring six ex-All Nippon passenger 767-200s for freighter conversion. UPS is expanding with a combination of new B-757 and B-767-300ER freighters while Federal Express Corp is buying converted passenger DC-10s and MD-11s as well as new A300-600Fs.
